summary: Audit the test suite to ensure all tests are run in CI checks, run consistently, no tests are improperly skipped, and `make test` runs all unit tests. The 20 orchestrator test files (~8800 lines) are completely excluded from CI and must be added. Pytest configuration is duplicated across pytest.ini and pyproject.toml and must be consolidated.

config_files: pyproject.toml [tool.pytest.ini_options] (testpaths=[tests], addopts with --cov flags but NO --tb=short)
test_infrastructure.config_precedence: pytest.ini takes precedence over pyproject.toml. CI command explicitly passes test directories and flags, bypassing both configs.

ci_workflows.test.yml: Unit tests (pytest tests/ gateway/tests/) + security scan (bandit)

test_infrastructure.make_test: Delegates to `act -j unit` which runs the test.yml unit job locally

test_directories.tests/: 83 test files - unit tests for sandbox, shared libs, action, config, gateway, security, scripts, tools, workflows, LLM
test_directories.gateway/tests/: 25 test files - gateway-specific unit tests with custom conftest import mangling
test_directories.orchestrator/tests/: 20 test files (~8800 lines) - orchestrator service tests (NOT in CI)
test_directories.integration_tests/: 13 test files - integration tests (require Docker/API tokens)
test_directories.integration_tests/local_pipeline/: 8 test files - pipeline orchestrator integration tests
test_directories.integration_tests/sdlc/: 6 test files - SDLC workflow integration tests

ci_coverage_config.coverage_with_orchestrator_added: ~71% (verified by risk analyst - WILL FAIL threshold)

findings.title: Orchestrator tests (20 files, ~8800 lines) completely excluded from CI
findings.description: orchestrator/tests/ is not included in any CI workflow. The test.yml unit job only runs `pytest tests/ gateway/tests/`. Regressions in orchestrator code are never caught in CI.

findings.title: Adding --cov=orchestrator breaks the 80% coverage threshold
findings.description: The risk analyst verified that combined coverage drops from ~80% to ~71% when orchestrator is included in --cov measurement. The orchestrator module has 10,321 uncovered lines. Adding --cov=orchestrator with --cov-fail-under=80 will break CI on every PR. MUST add orchestrator tests WITHOUT orchestrator coverage measurement initially.

findings.title: test_cli.py::test_serve_runs_as_non_root fails in combined pytest session
findings.description: When orchestrator tests run after tests/ and gateway/tests/ in a combined pytest session, test_serve_runs_as_non_root fails with 'TypeError: Logger._log() got an unexpected keyword argument host'. Root cause: orchestrator/cli.py line 84-88 calls logger.info() with keyword args (host=, port=, debug=). The EggLogger from shared/egg_logging accepts **kwargs in its _log method, but in a combined session there's a logger state interaction caused by gateway conftest.py's module loading and tests/conftest.py's sys.path manipulation. The test passes in isolation but fails in combined runs. This MUST be fixed before combining test directories in CI.

findings.title: pytest.ini and pyproject.toml both define testpaths (redundant config)
findings.description: Both files define test paths and options. pytest.ini takes precedence, making pyproject.toml's --cov addopts silently ignored for local pytest runs. CI overrides both. Should consolidate to pyproject.toml as single source of truth.

findings.title: Two orchestrator test files fail to collect without docker Python package
findings.description: test_container_spawner.py and test_docker_client.py fail collection because orchestrator/docker_client.py has `import docker` at module level. The docker package is in orchestrator/requirements.txt but NOT in pyproject.toml dev extras. CI uses `uv sync --extra dev` from pyproject.toml, so docker won't be installed. These files will cause 2 collection errors.

findings.title: Pre-existing gateway test failures in combined runs
findings.description: Two tests in gateway/tests/test_session_manager.py::TestSessionEndCheckpointCapture (test_capture_and_cleanup_handles_import_error, test_capture_and_cleanup_handles_capture_failure) fail in combined pytest sessions. These are pre-existing and not caused by adding orchestrator tests. Likely related to the same egg_logging interaction pattern. Should be documented as baseline context.

findings.title: PYTHONPATH must include orchestrator for combined test run
findings.description: Orchestrator tests use direct module imports (e.g., 'from models import Pipeline') which require the orchestrator/ directory on PYTHONPATH. Current CI PYTHONPATH is 'shared:gateway'. Must add 'orchestrator'.

findings.title: Intentionally skipped tests are legitimate
findings.description: 5 tests skip with 'Signals API not implemented', 1 skips with 'Decision timeout not supported' (feature gap placeholders). ~20 other pytest.skip() calls are environment-conditional (Docker, tokens, network). 2 xfail calls in test_agent_security_fuzz.py are appropriate. All are correct patterns.

findings.title: make test means unit tests only
findings.description: make test delegates to `act -j unit`. Integration/E2E tests require Docker and API tokens. Interpreting 'All tests should run when make test is run' as 'all unit tests' is pragmatic and correct.

recommended_approach.title: Add orchestrator tests to CI without coverage measurement, fix test interactions, consolidate config
recommended_approach.description: Four-phase approach: (1) Verify orchestrator tests pass standalone and fix the known test interaction, (2) Add orchestrator tests to CI WITHOUT --cov=orchestrator, (3) Consolidate pytest config, (4) Verify end-to-end. Coverage for orchestrator tracked separately as follow-up.

phases.baseline_context: Before starting, note that 2 pre-existing failures exist in gateway/tests/test_session_manager.py::TestSessionEndCheckpointCapture even without orchestrator tests. These are out of scope but should be documented.

tasks.title: Run orchestrator tests standalone and capture baseline
tasks.description: Run orchestrator tests in isolation to verify they pass. Expected: most tests pass, 2 collection errors from test_container_spawner.py and test_docker_client.py (docker package missing).
tasks.acceptance: All collectable orchestrator tests pass. 2 collection errors (docker-dependent files) identified.

tasks.title: Handle docker package collection errors
tasks.description: Two test files (test_container_spawner.py, test_docker_client.py) fail collection because orchestrator/docker_client.py imports docker at module level. The docker package is in orchestrator/requirements.txt but not in pyproject.toml dev extras. Resolution options: (a) Add docker>=7.0.0 to pyproject.toml [project.optional-dependencies] dev - this is the cleanest fix and ensures these tests run in CI. (b) If adding docker is undesirable (large dependency), add --ignore flags for these 2 files and document the exclusion.
tasks.recommended: Option (a): add docker>=7.0.0 to dev extras in pyproject.toml
tasks.acceptance: All 20 orchestrator test files collect successfully (0 collection errors) when running with `uv sync --extra dev`

tasks.title: Fix test_cli.py logging interaction for combined runs
tasks.description: test_serve_runs_as_non_root fails in combined pytest sessions (tests/ gateway/tests/ orchestrator/tests/) because orchestrator/cli.py calls logger.info() with keyword arguments (host=, port=, debug=) that only work with EggLogger, not standard logging.Logger. In combined sessions, the logger state is affected by gateway conftest.py's module loading (which loads modules via exec()) and tests/conftest.py's sys.path manipulation. The fix should ensure test_cli.py works regardless of logger type. Two approaches: (a) Mock the logger in the test to avoid depending on global logging state. This is the safest fix - the test should mock cli.logger to prevent the keyword-argument call from reaching a real logger. (b) In cli.py, wrap the logger.info() call to use standard logging format (passing host/port/debug via extra= dict instead of kwargs). This is a production code change and may be out of scope for a test audit.
tasks.recommended: Option (a): Mock cli.logger in test_serve_runs_as_non_root to isolate it from logging state. Add `with patch('cli.logger') as mock_logger:` inside the test.
tasks.acceptance: Combined pytest command passes: PYTHONPATH=shared:gateway:orchestrator pytest tests/ gateway/tests/ orchestrator/tests/ -v (test_serve_runs_as_non_root does not fail)

tasks.title: Fix any other failing orchestrator tests
tasks.description: After TASK-1-2 and TASK-1-3, run the full combined suite and fix any remaining failures. The risk analyst noted orchestrator tests have 450 passing and the test_serve_runs_as_non_root as the only interaction failure.
tasks.acceptance: PYTHONPATH=shared:gateway:orchestrator pytest tests/ gateway/tests/ orchestrator/tests/ -v exits 0 (excluding pre-existing gateway failures)

tasks.title: Migrate pytest.ini settings into pyproject.toml
tasks.description: Move all settings from pytest.ini to pyproject.toml [tool.pytest.ini_options]: (1) markers: integration, functional, e2e, security, agent_flaky. (2) filterwarnings: ignore::DeprecationWarning. (3) python_files, python_classes, python_functions patterns. (4) testpaths: update to ['tests', 'gateway/tests', 'orchestrator/tests']. (5) addopts: update to include --tb=short (from pytest.ini) AND existing --cov flags. The combined addopts should be: '-v --tb=short --cov=gateway --cov=shared --cov=sandbox --cov-report=term-missing'. Note: Do NOT add --cov=orchestrator to addopts for the same reason as TASK-2-1. Do NOT add --cov-fail-under to addopts (it's only in CI to avoid blocking local development).

technical_decisions.decision: Do NOT add --cov=orchestrator to CI coverage measurement
technical_decisions.rationale: Risk analyst verified combined coverage drops to ~71% with orchestrator, failing the 80% threshold. Adding orchestrator tests to CI execution without coverage measurement allows catching regressions without breaking CI. Orchestrator coverage will be added incrementally as a follow-up.
alternatives_considered: Lower --cov-fail-under to 70% (rejected: removes coverage gate for all modules, too risky)
Write enough orchestrator tests to reach 80% in this PR (rejected: 10,321 uncovered lines makes this unrealistic for a test audit)

technical_decisions.decision: Fix test_cli.py interaction by mocking the logger in the test
technical_decisions.rationale: The test_serve_runs_as_non_root test fails in combined runs due to logger state interaction. Mocking cli.logger in the test is the safest fix — it doesn't require production code changes and isolates the test from global logging state. Alternative of changing cli.py's logging call is a production code change that may be out of scope.
alternatives_considered: Run orchestrator tests in separate pytest invocation in CI (rejected: adds CI complexity, masks the real issue)
Change cli.py to use standard logging format (rejected: production code change out of scope for test audit)

technical_decisions.decision: Add docker>=7.0.0 to pyproject.toml dev extras
technical_decisions.rationale: The docker package is already a runtime dependency of the orchestrator (in orchestrator/requirements.txt). Adding it to dev extras ensures the 2 docker-dependent test files (test_container_spawner.py, test_docker_client.py) can be collected and run in CI. The alternative of using --ignore flags means these tests never run in CI, which contradicts the audit goal.
alternatives_considered: Add --ignore flags for docker-dependent test files (rejected: defeats purpose of audit)
Guard docker import with try/except in docker_client.py (rejected: production code change)

technical_decisions.decision: Consolidate to pyproject.toml, preserve --tb=short from pytest.ini
technical_decisions.rationale: pyproject.toml is the modern standard for Python project config. The current pyproject.toml addopts is missing --tb=short that pytest.ini has. When consolidating, both --tb=short and existing --cov flags must be preserved in the merged addopts.

Integration/E2E tests require Docker and API tokens. 'All tests should run when make test is run' is interpreted as 'all unit tests'. This is pragmatic and consistent with the existing test infrastructure design.

technical_decisions.decision: Do not remove conditional skips in integration tests
technical_decisions.rationale: The ~20 conditional pytest.skip() calls for Docker/token/network availability are correct patterns. They allow the same test suite to run in different environments gracefully.
